title: Microsoft 365 Backup: activity logs for policy and restore operations
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the navigation, commands, permissions, retention and published Backup pricing. It correctly distinguishes operational logs from Purview Audit and reports the different roadmap and Message Center schedules rather than silently choosing one.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn directs compliance investigations requiring the Microsoft 365 audit record to Purview Audit rather than in-product activity logs.
claims.quote: For compliance investigations that require the Microsoft 365 audit record, continue to use Microsoft Purview Audit.

claims.claim: Audit > Search is the documented search route in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote:
1. Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal.
2. Select the Audit solution card.
3. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start> -EndDate <end> -Operations BackupPolicyActivated searches the unified audit log for that operation.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    [-Operations <String[]>]
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: Audit searches require the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log.

claims.claim: For users with non-E5 Office 365 or Microsoft 365 licences, audit records are retained for 180 days.
claims.quote: For users assigned any other (non-E5) Office 365 or Microsoft 365 license, the system retains audit records for 180 days.

claims.claim: For users with E5 licences, Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange and SharePoint audit activity is retained for one year by default.
claims.quote: the system retains audit records for Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, and SharePoint activity for one year by default.

claims.quote: | Activated a Backup Policy | BackupPolicyActivated | A Microsoft 365 Backup policy is activated from an inactive state. |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate activity-log licence, meter or charge is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs separate license pricing charge meter. Opened Learn backup-pricing, backup-overview, backup-privacy-security, backup-whats-new and Graph list activityLogs; read MC1489931 and roadmap. None names a separate activity-log licence, meter or charge.

claims.claim: Learn's activity-log section lists required roles but no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs separate license pricing charge meter. Read the complete Activity logs section of Learn backup-privacy-security, including Required roles; it lists administrator roles and no licence.

claims.claim: Learn documents no setting that turns activity logs on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs enable disable setting policy permissions roles access. Opened backup-privacy-security and Graph list activityLogs; read backup-setup and Entra role search excerpts. No activity-log enable/disable setting was found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn describes no action on the activity-log page that changes a backup policy or restore.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs page assign roles grant access change policy restore action. Read backup-privacy-security Activity logs and Graph list activityLogs. They document viewing, filtering, searching and exporting, not changing policies or restores.

claims.where: Governance controls; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Activity-log access follows existing administrator workload permissions rather than being granted by opening the logs page.
claims.quote: Role-based access controls will apply. Administrators will only be able to view logs for workloads they are authorized to manage.

claims.claim: The in-product capability is for Microsoft 365 Backup and offers SharePoint, Exchange and OneDrive as service options.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Backup Activity Logs provide an in-product view of backup policy and restore operations.
Service options can be SharePoint, Exchange or OneDrive.

claims.claim: Learn states the ceiling and retention but does not explain limit handling or whether pre-rollout history appears.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup activity logs 1 million limit oldest history before rollout. Opened backup-privacy-security and backup-whats-new; read Graph list activityLogs and MC1489931. No behaviour at the ceiling or guarantee of pre-rollout history was found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Activity logs become available to the relevant Backup administrators without an enablement action.
claims.quote:
Activity logs will be available for Microsoft 365 Backup actions across supported workloads, including SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and Exchange Online.
No action is required.
